body.query:
_GetWatchlist("YOUR_WATCHLIST")

INSERT INTO PasswordFiles (
    IncidentNumber,
    FilePath,
    UserPrincipalName,
    UserObjectID,
    ContactDate,
    Operator,
    OurAction,
    TheirResponse
)
SELECT 
    '@{body('Parse_JSON_-_Incident_body')?['object']?['properties']?['incidentNumber']}', -- IncidentNumber
    @FilePath, -- FilePath
    '@{variables('String-AccountEmail')}', -- UserPrincipalName
    '', -- UserObjectID
    GETDATE(), -- ContactDate (The time the contact action is logged)
    '@{triggerBody()?['object']?['properties']?['owner']?['email']}', -- Operator
    'Emailed relevant parties about the incident and policy.', -- OurAction
    '' -- TheirResponse
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    
    -- --- LOGIC 1: SIMPLE 7-DAY LOOKBACK (Relative to NOW) ---
    -- Do not insert if ANY existing entry for this user/file has a ContactDate less than 7 days old.
    SELECT 1
    FROM PasswordFiles AS PF_Simple
    WHERE PF_Simple.FilePath = @FilePath
    AND PF_Simple.UserPrincipalName = '@{variables('String-AccountEmail')}'
    AND PF_Simple.ContactDate >= DATEADD(day, -7, GETDATE())
    
    -- --- OR LOGIC 2: ADVANCED INCIDENT DATE CHECK (Relative to Incident Creation Time) ---
    -- Do not insert if the incident creation date is within 7 days of the LATEST contact date.
    OR EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM PasswordFiles AS InnerPF
        WHERE InnerPF.FilePath = @FilePath
        AND InnerPF.UserPrincipalName = '@{variables('String-AccountEmail')}'
        
        -- Aggregate and find the MAX (most recent) ContactDate for the pair
        GROUP BY InnerPF.FilePath, InnerPF.UserPrincipalName
        
        -- Filter the group: Check if the MAX ContactDate is recent enough
        HAVING MAX(InnerPF.ContactDate) >= DATEADD(day, -7, '@{formatDateTime(triggerBody()?['object']?['properties']?['createdTimeUtc'], 'yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ')}')
    )
);

SELECT @@ROWCOUNT AS RowsAffected;

body.content:
Hi @{variables('String-AccountEmail')},

I am @{split(triggerBody()?['object']?['properties']?['owner']?['assignedTo'],', ')[1]}, a YOUR_JOB_TITLE from Digital Security Operations.

I am writing to you on behalf of my team regarding a compliance issue that has been brought to our attention. It has been observed that a SharePoint/OneDrive file(s) containing credential(s) has been accessed on @{split(body('Parse_JSON_-_Incident_body')?['object']?['properties']?['createdTimeUtc'],'T')[0]}.

File(s):
@{concat('
  • ', replace(join(variables('Array-URLs'), '
  • '), ' ', '%20'), '
')}

Please do not store any form of credentials on SharePoint/OneDrive as it poses a significant security risk.

Action Required:
  • Remove the file(s) and relocate credential(s) to an approved, secure credential manager (e.g., YOUR_PASSWORD_MANAGER or Edge Password Manager).
  • If the file(s) contains non-sensitive information (no actual credentials), rename it to avoid false alarms.
  • If the encrypted file(s) contains sensitive information and its filename provides hints for the password/passcode, rename it.
  • If the sensitive file(s) is essential to be stored on OneDrive/SharePoint, encrypt it with a password that is stored elsewhere (e.g., YOUR_PASSWORD_MANAGER).
  • If you are not responsible for the file(s) involved, please let us know who we should contact for follow-ups.

Please address this issue with urgency. If you require any guidance or have questions regarding this process, do not hesitate to contact us.

Please visit the following link for more information about the policies:
DDAT Policies and Procedures

Thank you!
